title: Round 2 for akshaisrin.live
question: Robotics-grounded, wow without overdoing it. The roll assigned Perception Overlay; Kinematic Blueprint is my pick. Choose, or re-roll.

options.label: Perception Overlay
options.lineage: AV and robot perception debug views (detections, tracks, depth)
options.thesis: The site is what the robot sees: real photographs annotated live by a perception stack, with the resume as a multi-object tracking timeline.
materials: mono HUD readouts on neutral instrument chrome
options.viewport: A full-bleed real photo of Akshai. On load a perception pass runs once: a hairline box draws around him, the label types in as PERSON 0.99 then resolves to AKSHAI SRINIVASAN, keypoints land, the mask fills. Top HUD strip: frame counter, timestamp 2026-08-27, camera FRONT_CENTER, and two actions, RESUME.PDF and EMAIL. Beside the box, an attributes panel in mono: role MLE Intern @ GM Cruise, edu CE + AMATH @ UW, org DubHacks Director of Technology. A three-way layer switch, RGB / DEPTH / SEG, re-renders every image on the site. Scrolling annotates each section's imagery as it enters. Experience is a tracking timeline: each org a track with a real start and end, current roles marked LIVE. Projects are detections shelved by class: ROBOTICS & RL, SYSTEMS & INFRA, GAMES & PLAY. The BDX duck is detected as DROID 0.97; a boba cup gets its own box. On phones the photo crops portrait and the HUD moves to the bottom.
options.risk: Boxes on photos is a familiar AI-company trope; it survives only with real photographs, overlays authored per image with true geometry, and one pass per image, never a screen full of boxes. Confidence values are the form's grammar and must never read as claims about people or work. Needs two to four real photos from you: with hardware, at DubHacks, in the lab.

raised.raise: Registration is visible: the layer legend (RGB / DEPTH / SEG) and registration crosses stay in the margin on every annotated image.
Prose gets a clearing: the About paragraph and every body text sits in clean, unannotated space; overlays stop at the image edge.
A NOW marker never leaves the screen: the HUD's frame counter and timestamp always say where you are, and current roles read LIVE.
Mobile collapse discipline: annotations fold to their box outline and reopen on tap.
Multi-track sync: the experience timeline stacks orgs as time-aligned channels, like sensor tracks in one log.

regions.label: HUD: frame · timestamp · camera · RESUME.PDF · EMAIL

options.label: Kinematic Blueprint
options.lineage: URDF / engineering drawings of robot arms with joint frames and a title block
options.thesis: The site is the engineering drawing of a six-axis arm whose joints are the sections; scrolling articulates the chain.
options.viewport: A six-axis arm drawn in line art across the whole sheet, joint frames J1 to J6 labeled with xyz triads; each joint is a section (About, Experience, Projects, Skills, Resume, Contact). Bottom-right, a real engineering title block: TITLE Akshai Srinivasan, ROLE MLE Intern @ GM Cruise, EDU CE + AMATH @ UW, ORG DubHacks Dir. of Technology, DATE 2026-08, REV 3, with RESUME.PDF and EMAIL as title-block fields. Scrolling rotates the joints; the arm reaches each section.
options.risk: Blueprint aesthetics are a known trope and this is where many engineering portfolios land; if the arm does not actually articulate it is a poster.

regions.label: six-axis arm line drawing with joint frames
title block: name · role · edu · RESUME · EMAIL

options.label: Technical Zine
options.thesis: The playful streak at full volume: marker headlines, doodled diagrams, a mascot, and highlighter swipes teaching who Akshai is.
options.viewport: A marker headline with the name, a doodled robot arm diagram with looping arrows to the three roles, a sketched table of contents down the side.
options.case: Instantly readable and warm, but you chose professional with a streak, and cream plus marker reads student project to a recruiter.
options.risk: Cream paper and marker is a rut of its own; the mascot has to be drawn well or it is clip art.

options.label: Screenprint Overlap
options.thesis: Sections as translucent cyan, amber, and scarlet passes that mix where they overlap.
options.viewport: The name as a stencil banner, roles as overprinted passes drifting out of register.
options.case: No robotics reading and overprint ghosts hurt scanability.
options.kept: Registration marks and a visible layer legend.

options.label: Secession Page
options.thesis: A folk-flower border grows in from the margins around one calm column.
options.viewport: Ornament growing inward around the name and a single column of prose.
options.case: Beautiful and unrelated to an engineer; nobody in the audience identifies.
options.kept: Prose sits in a clearing, never overlaid.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.thesis: The resume as sixteen candy-colored steps under a chase light.
options.viewport: A step row timeline with the chase light on now.
options.case: Musicians identify, recruiters do not; the metaphor says nothing about robotics.
options.kept: A NOW marker that never leaves the screen.

options.label: Akari Workshop
options.thesis: Sections as glowing paper volumes in a dim room.
options.viewport: Warm paper moons hanging at different heights, the name brush-stamped.
options.case: Serene and meaningless for this product.
options.kept: Small screens collapse volumes to outlines that reopen on tap.

options.label: Rain-Night Cityscape
options.thesis: Seattle at night, transit veins and wet-street reflections as the ground.
options.viewport: A skyline band, a street band, a reflection band; the name in neon lettering.
options.case: AV people half-identify, but a city nocturne says nothing about Akshai and it is the dark-and-glow rut again.
options.kept: Time-aligned stacked bands, like sensor tracks in one log.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer portfolio this category ships, executed impeccably: name, typed roles, social icons, card grid.
canonCard.viewport: Centered name and one-line identity, social row, sections stacked below with a card grid of projects.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other CS student portfolio by design.
